hook: This tower once tested Saturn V moon rockets. Then it came down.
narration: This tower once tested fully assembled Saturn V moon rockets. Then it came down.
It was the Dynamic Test Stand at NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, built in 1964.
In 1978, engineers put all the space shuttle elements together there for the first time.
Nearby stood the T-tower, built in 1957 by the Army Ballistic Missile Agency.
Its tests helped develop the Saturn family of rockets, and it last fired shuttle solid rocket motors in the 1990s.
In an implosion, small charges cut the key supports in sequence, so gravity pulls the structure down into its own footprint.
On January tenth, 2026, the T-tower went first.
Its steel frame dropped straight down into its own dust.
[short pause] Then the charges went off inside the Dynamic Test Stand.
outcome: Both historic test stands came down, clearing room for a campus built for the next era of space exploration.
title: Saturn V test tower comes down
description:
NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, removed two historic test stands, the Propulsion and Structural Test Facility and the Dynamic Test Facility, with coordinated implosions on Jan. 10, 2026.
